reviews.feedback: I like that the skills continues to ask questions until has the context clear, and then start writing the post, i like the fact that if the answers still dont clarify the context enough the skill keeps asking more specific questions before writing the post. That's exactly the approach i was looking for. But something i dont like is when a question is too specific, like "3. **Can you share a specific piece of code where the architecture decision mattered?** Something like: a use case class that felt right, a repository interface that simplified testing, or a spot where following the dependency rule saved you when swapping an adapter. Conversely, was there a place where the layering felt like unnecessary ceremony?" I think providing a specific piece of code adds nothing and for me it is a blocking question, it forces me to lose a lot of time to answer to get not really much.

The thing i dont like about this result is the writing style with the iper short phrases, i tend to prefer simple but medium long phrases, that articulate more the explaination and the thought process behind what im sharing, i dont want to just be factual, but integrate more complexity keeping the text very simple to understand to almost anyone. I also want to integrate some parallelisms between programming and philosophy and life in general

Here i noticed that u used a lot the pattern i dont like consisting in: not because this but this, or not this, but this, ecc... I just want to share my experience in a relaxed way, i dont have any interest in resulting a guru or in adding pathos to the post, just keep it very chill
